learningObjectives: Explain the role of a TestSheet within the TestCase Design section.
Create and structure Attributes to represent the business objects and behaviors under test.
Separate nested Attribute structure from the user-controlled BusinessRelevant setting.
Use an independently proposed Administration, Precondition, Process and Verification layout.

elements.description: A TestSheet organizes logical test data. The documentation recommends covering each Requirement with a TestSheet; creating a sheet alone does not prove its generated tests fully cover the criterion.

A characteristic or business object involved in the behavior being tested — for example, a credit-card drop-down on a checkout form. Attributes describe *what varies*; the specific values an Attribute can take (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) are added later as Instances (Lesson 3).
Like Requirements, Attributes can be layered — every Attribute may have sub-Attributes, depending on how much detail the TestSheet needs.

bulletPoints: TestSheets can use Attributes for data-oriented design or Steps for process-oriented design.
Attribute = the characteristic; Instance (next lesson) = the specific value of that characteristic.

elements.description: Attributes can contain sub-Attributes and Instances. BusinessRelevant separately identifies input relevance or verification data. The accessed 2026.1 pages do not establish the earlier lesson’s claim about a non-editable AttrType property; do not rely on that unverified UI rule.

bulletPoints: A parent Attribute can group details without making them separate executable TestSteps.
Confirm any additional property behavior against your installed version.

elements.description: Independent Quilyn organizational example: group metadata, setup, inputs and expected results under four named Attributes when that makes a TestSheet easier to understand. These exact names are not a mandatory or verified universal Tricentis recommendation.

elements.title: Administration / Precondition / Process / Verification
items: Administration — metadata about the TestCase itself (designer, contact person, test stage, comments). Not actual test data, and not business relevant.
Precondition — prerequisite data needed to get the application/workspace into the right starting state (e.g. login credentials). Required to run, but not the focus of the test.
Process — the actual data being tested; directly relevant to the TestCase's purpose.
Verification — data used to check whether the process behaved as expected; comparison/expected-result values.

bulletPoints: Administration = context, not test data. Precondition = setup. Process = what's under test. Verification = expected outcome.

elements.description: BusinessRelevant is user-controlled. Yes is the default; No identifies non-relevant data and Result identifies verification data. Changing the parent setting also changes its sub-Attributes.

elements.title: Yes / No / Result
items: Yes — input data relevant to the test; default.
No — metadata not relevant to the test.
Result — expected or comparison data for verification.

elements.text: Setting BusinessRelevant on a parent Attribute propagates that value down to all of its sub-Attributes.

bulletPoints: Map the four core Attributes to BusinessRelevant like this: Administration=No, Precondition=Yes, Process=Yes, Verification=Result.

elements.title: Create a TestSheet
items: Right-click the destination folder and choose Create TestSheet.
Rename it; TestSheet names must be unique within that folder.
The overview documents Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T for a TestSheet.

elements.title: Create an Attribute
items: Right-click its containing object and choose Create Attribute.
Use a unique name. Dot, right-arrow and left-arrow characters are removed from Attribute names.
The overview documents Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A for an Attribute.

elements.text: Toggle Business Relevance in the ribbon or with Ctrl+F7. Inspect the resulting BusinessRelevant value and descendants; the icon color also indicates relevance.
Independent Quilyn notes based on the linked documentation. Original Academy video/exercise numbering could not be inspected because the course requires authentication.

bulletPoints: Independent recommendation: keep names and folder organization consistent with your criteria for traceability.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing nesting with relevance
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming parent/child structure by itself determines whether data is a relevant input or expected result.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Nested Attributes organize characteristics; BusinessRelevant independently specifies Yes, No or Result. Additional AttrType UI behavior is not verified by the accessed documentation.

examPitfalls.title: Leaving Administration as BusinessRelevant = Yes
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Forgetting to set the Administration Attribute's business relevance, so metadata like 'Test Designer' gets pulled into combinatorics.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Administration should be set to BusinessRelevant = No, since it holds context/metadata, not data that should influence which combinations are generated.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing Precondition and Process
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Placing the actual data under test inside Precondition, or setup/login data inside Process.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Precondition holds prerequisite setup data (not the test's focus, e.g. login info); Process holds the data that is actually the focus of the TestCase.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming BusinessRelevant settings apply per-Attribute only
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Manually re-setting BusinessRelevant on every sub-Attribute after already setting it on the parent.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: BusinessRelevant set on a parent Attribute automatically propagates to all of its sub-Attributes — no need to repeat it lower in the tree.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Credit Card' Attribute contains card number, expiry date and card type. Which statement describes this TestCase-Design structure?

options.text: It must be a physical browser Module because it describes a card.
It is a parent Attribute grouping sub-Attributes for related characteristics.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Attributes describe characteristics and can contain further Attributes or Instances. Grouping card details under one parent is a logical design structure, not a scanned browser Module.

optionExplanations.A: TestCase-Design Attributes are not scanned Module controls.
optionExplanations.B: A parent can group related child characteristics.
optionExplanations.C: The documentation permits Attributes within Attributes.
optionExplanations.D: The proposed restriction contradicts the documented hierarchy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the independent four-group layout, which documented BusinessRelevant value fits expected outcomes in Verification?
practiceQuiz.hint: This value flags an Attribute as holding comparison/expected-outcome data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Verification is typically set to BusinessRelevant = Result, indicating it holds data used for verifications/comparisons rather than data that should drive combinatorics.

optionExplanations.A: Yes identifies relevant data, not the explicit verification role asked here.
optionExplanations.B: No identifies data not relevant to the test, rather than expected comparison data.
optionExplanations.C: Result is the documented verification-data value.
optionExplanations.D: Verification data does use the BusinessRelevant property.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester sets the top-level Administration Attribute's BusinessRelevant to 'No'. What happens to its sub-Attributes (e.g. 'Test Designer', 'Comments')?

options.text: Nothing — each sub-Attribute must be set individually.
They automatically inherit BusinessRelevant = No from the parent.
They automatically switch to AttrType = Physical.

practiceQuiz.hint: BusinessRelevant is a property that flows down the tree.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Setting BusinessRelevant on a parent Attribute propagates that setting to all of its sub-Attributes automatically.

optionExplanations.A: The parent change applies to its sub-Attributes.
optionExplanations.B: Descendants adopt the parent’s business relevance.
optionExplanations.C: Changing relevance does not delete Attributes.
optionExplanations.D: Relevance changes do not redefine the nested structure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which shortcut creates a new Attribute directly (without using the Ribbon or right-click menu)?
practiceQuiz.hint: T is for TestSheet, R is for Requirement — this one is for the object covered in this lesson.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The overview documents Ctrl+N, Ctrl+A for creating an Attribute and Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T for a TestSheet. Ctrl+F7 toggles Business Relevance; it does not create an Attribute.

optionExplanations.A: This creates a TestSheet, not an Attribute.
optionExplanations.B: This is not the documented Attribute-creation shortcut.
optionExplanations.C: The overview lists this sequence for Attributes.
optionExplanations.D: This toggles business relevance rather than creating an object.

quickRecap.value: Organizes logical test data; creation alone does not certify Requirement coverage.
A characteristic/business object; can have sub-Attributes.
Attributes can contain Attributes or Instances; BusinessRelevant independently denotes relevance or expected results. Additional AttrType behavior unverified.
Independent layout: Administration (No), Precondition/Process (Yes), Verification (Result). Not an enforced product template.
Yes / No / Result — user-set, propagates to sub-Attributes, controls inclusion in combinatorics.
